explain.say: A cloud is made of billions of tiny water droplets or ice crystals floating in the air. It starts when the Sun warms water and turns it into invisible water vapour.

faq.q: Where does the water in a cloud come from?
faq.a: From evaporation: the Sun warms oceans, lakes, soil and plants, and water escapes into the air as invisible vapour. Most of it comes from the oceans.
asks: How does water get into the sky?

faq.q: Why does rising air cool down?
faq.a: Higher up there is less air pressing in, so a rising pocket of air expands. Expanding uses some of its energy, so it cools, about 10 degrees Celsius per kilometre for dry air.
asks: Why is it colder where clouds form?

faq.a: Water vapour needs a surface to condense on. Tiny specks of dust, sea salt, pollen or smoke, called condensation nuclei, give it somewhere to gather into droplets.
The dew point is the temperature at which air becomes full of water vapour, so any more cooling makes vapour condense into droplets. Clouds form where rising air cools to its dew point.

faq.q: Why do clouds have flat bottoms?
faq.a: The flat base marks the height where rising air first cools to its dew point. Below that height the air stays clear; above it, droplets form.
asks: Why is the bottom of a cloud flat?

facts: A typical cloud droplet is about 0.02 millimetres across, far too small to fall quickly.
A fluffy cumulus cloud can hold hundreds of tonnes of water.

quiz.say: What do water droplets in a cloud form around?

options.show: Tiny specks of dust, salt or smoke
options.say: Tiny specks of dust, salt or smoke

quiz.why: Water vapour needs a surface to condense on, and tiny particles called condensation nuclei provide it.

wrong.1: Oxygen is a gas mixed through the air; it does not give vapour a surface to gather on.
wrong.2: Hailstones only form inside big storm clouds, long after the cloud has formed.
